title: Alert weighting + circuit-orchestration for noisy multi-region paths
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Pager noise has increased over the last quarter because transient network flaps and region-local infra degradation are triggering full-fidelity on-call pages. This is causing fatigue, slower mean-time-to-acknowledge, and unnecessary failovers. We need a combined approach: (1) smarter alert scoring/weighting so only high-confidence incidents page, (2) cross-region circuit orchestration that can fail-over or fail-open gracefully, and (3) automated incident runbook triggers that perform safe mitigation steps before human paging for medium-severity signals.

Goals:
- Reduce actionable pages from noisy, high-cardinality monitors by 60% without increasing customer-visible SLO breaches.
- Implement a score-based paging system that combines multiple signals (error rate, error budget burn, trip frequency, KV-cache miss deltas, and region adjacency) to determine paging vs. ticket creation only.
- Orchestrate circuit-breaker state across regions so that transient region-level circuits can enter degraded mode (fail-open to warm fallback model or reduced QPS) rather than immediate global failover.
- Implement automation hooks that run a validated mitigation playbook (cache flush, routing weight shift, restart pool) for medium-confidence incidents for up to 10 minutes before escalating to an on-call page.

Design notes (high level):
- Signals used for scoring: 5xx rate (p95/p99), latency p99, region-specific error budget burn rate (1h and 6h windows), circuit-trip count, KV-cache miss-rate spike, downstream dependency error spread, and anomaly score from our model. Each signal maps to a numeric weight; weights are tunable via console.
- Score calculation: weighted sum normalized to 0-100. Thresholds: 0-29 -> ticket-only (no page), 30-59 -> automated remediation + ticket, 60+ -> immediate page with remediation.
- Circuit orchestration: each region runs a circuit with local health. A new control-plane component (circuit-orchestrator) will maintain soft-state mirroring of region circuits and enforce policies: local degrade (reduce qps, enable quantized model), cascade-protect (prevent global failover unless >70% of regions report critical), and quorum promotions for failover.
- Automation: remediation runbooks are atomic, idempotent actions executed by the IRTbot (Runbook Runner). Examples: scale up model pool 2x, switch traffic to warm-standby model variant, increase batching window, selectively enable token-level caching. Runbook actions have safety checks and rollback steps.
- Paging integration: Datadog -> score engine -> PagerDuty. The score engine will be implemented as a lightweight service (Go) that subscribes to metrics via the metrics ingest stream and to monitor events. It will annotate and modify monitor actions via tags/metadata and call PagerDuty API for paging decisions.

Acceptance criteria:
- A/B test over two weeks shows >=60% reduction in noisy pages for monitors in the test cohort and no increase in SLO misses at the customer-facing level.
- Circuit-orchestrator deployed to staging and configured for two staging regions; failover policy correctly prevents global failover when only one region degrades.
- A documented set of 6 automated playbooks exist in our runbook library with unit tests and dry-run mode.
- PagerDuty escalation policies updated to consume score engine outputs and route pages only when thresholds are met.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement score engine prototype and run in shadow mode for 2 weeks (monitor alert volumes but do not change paging).
2) Author and validate runbooks for common mitigations in staging; create dry-run automation tests.
3) Deploy circuit-orchestrator in canary to 1 region pair; run synthetic failure drills.
4) Flip score engine to active for non-critical monitors with automation-first policy for 50% of traffic.
5) Measure, iterate weights, expand to all regional monitors, then to critical monitors.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Score engine mis-classifies a genuine incident and delays pages -> mitigation: conservative thresholds initially and a fallback health-check that can override score if absolute customer errors exceed hard limits.
- Risk: Runbook automation introduces churn -> mitigation: require dry-run test, safety gates, and a manual-confirm mode for high-impact actions.
